blocks.md: Identification asks whether the data can, even in principle, tell different explanations apart. In regression it fails when one explanatory variable is an exact combination of others — say total income alongside its two components, labor income and non-labor income. Then you can shift weight between the variables without changing any prediction, so infinitely many sets of coefficients fit equally well and the regression cannot pick one. Full rank is the condition that rules this out.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: Without it the computer either refuses to run the regression or silently drops a variable, and any coefficient you get has no meaning.

sections.heading: The dummy variable trap is this condition

blocks.md: With all $k$ dummies plus an intercept, the dummy columns sum exactly to the column of ones. See [Indicator Variables](note:indicator-variables).

The lecture's general statement: it is not possible, within the model, for two different parameter sets to produce the same $E[y\mid\mathbf{x}]$ **for all** $\mathbf{x}$ vectors. (It is possible for *some* $\mathbf{x}$.)
